questions.q: What do the four letters in the Cashflow Quadrant stand for?
a: Employee, self-employed, business owner, investor
Earner, saver, borrower, spender
Employee, supervisor, broker, inheritor
Entrepreneur, specialist, banker, insurer
questions.why: The overview lists the four types as employee, self-employed, business owner and investor, labeled E, S, B and I.

questions.q: What separates the E and S quadrants from the B and I quadrants?
a: The first two trade time for money; the last two own income-producing assets
The first two pay fewer taxes; the last two pay more
The first two take big risks; the last two play it safe
The first two need more schooling; the last two need less
questions.why: Lesson 1 says E and S workers rely on their own labor, while B and I people build assets and keep improving how they work.

questions.q: Why does the summary say owning a business builds wealth faster?
a: You keep more of your income and the company's profits
You can avoid paying any taxes at all
You never have to work again
You can dismiss employees without cause
questions.why: Lesson 2 points to lower taxes and keeping the profits of a business you own.

questions.q: Which type of investor does the summary say you should aim to become?
a: The professional investor who studies the market
The saver who avoids risk altogether
The busy investor who hands money to an expert
The investor with little financial knowledge
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes the professional investor as the ideal, one who analyzes opportunities and keeps educating themselves.

questions.q: What is the capitalist investor in the summary?
a: A business owner who invests profits to make more
Someone who only buys government bonds
A consultant who manages other people's money
An employee with a large retirement fund
questions.why: Lesson 3 calls the capitalist investor the biggest player, owning a business and investing its profits for further returns.
